limits: Post-detection selection biases all estimates. Metrics do not independently validate a signal or determine its origin.
Barycentric coherence may describe absorption/emission blends or instrumental structure; no stellar-rest-frame identity follows.
Topocentric coherence is not proof of terrestrial origin.
Multiple hit records and nearby centers are correlated and cannot be counted as independent phenomena.
Temporal repeats are archival exposures,not independent new telescope observations.
No significance calibration,survey completeness,physical line flux,or extraterrestrial claim.
New epochs are archival observations, not observations commissioned by this project; records and nearby event centers remain correlated.
New BERV range alone does not identify physical origin or give a sensitivity/false-alarm calibration.
Instrument era, pipeline, extraction/blaze/background, line-spread function and wavelength zero-point may differ even when nominal units/resolution match.
Original discovery ERR samples are unavailable; inherited fits are unweighted and errors are descriptive only, even if a new product supplies positive errors.
Signed Gaussian widths are fixed templates, not measured linewidths. Normalized amplitudes are not calibrated fluxes or significance.
Barycentric wavelengths are not a stellar rest frame; stellar radial-velocity changes remain a potential confounder.
Partial/missing/incompatible products remain explicit blocked selected slots; no replacement target or epoch is chosen from flux outcomes.
